newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 17.

text.p: A defence investigation into sexual abuse and harassment of female ratings on the frigate Wellington has been criticised as inadequate as new complaints have been made. Labour MP Ross Robertson on Sunday night accused navy personnel of "threats and intimidation" against women who had alleged sexual harassment during their time on the frigate. Page 1.

Labour MP Mike Moore has applied to Speaker Doug Kidd for Parliament to hold an urgent debate on Tuesday on the future of race relations. He said on Sunday that deteriorating race relations would boil over unless Parliament took control. "Parliament must discuss it now, or will we discuss it when someone is killed? Someone will get hurt, there's no doubt about that," Moore said. Page 1.

A call to decide the future of the five Maori seats through a public referendum has been dismissed by senior Maori MPs. The call comes from ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble, who said the separate Maori seats were "dangerous" and unnecessary under MMP. Page 2.

ACT NZ MP Muriel Newman has rejected accusations that she was insensitive in sending a Taupo widow humorous budget advice. Newman, ACT's social welfare spokeswoman, responded to a letter last year from the widow, 59, who was having trouble making ends meet, by sending extracts from a book she co-wrote, How to Live
on the Smell of an Oily Rag. Page 2.

Two leading ACT NZ MPs have given opposing views on race relations in New Zealand. Donna Awatere Huata told delegates at the party's annual conference in Auckland at the weekend that "race relations have never been better, and I'm telling you this as someone who has been at the front line of race relations in this country for the past 30 years". However, former National cabinet minister Derek Quigley said New Zealand was fast losing its way in race relations terms. Page 2.

Economic activity fell in Wellington in the last three months of 1996, the only region in the North Island to suffer a decline, the National Bank says. But during the whole of 1996, Wellington was the second highest performer, with economic growth of 4.1 percent, just behind Northland with 4.8 percent, according to a National Bank regional survey released on Monday. Page 19.

An abnormal $4.37 million cost associated with litigation over the Martha Hill goldmine at Waihi plunged Otter Gold Mines $1.96 million into the red in the December 31 half-year. In March, Otter received a High Court judgment payment of $4.14 million from a legal action against Poseidon Gold (Posgold), which was brought to account as revenue at June 30, 1996. The litigation concerned Posgold's acquisition of Amax Gold's interest in Martha Hill. Page 19.

The findings of a liquor law review are expected to be revealed at the end of the week. An advisory committee assessed more than 400 submissions on 13 issues, ranging from Sunday trading to the minimum drinking age on licensed premises. The committee reviewing the Sale of Liquor Act 1989 is chaired by former Ombudsman Sir John Robertson. Page 19.

Established manufacturer and exporter Gilbert Ullrich of Ullrich Aluminium is stirring up opposition to the Manufacturers Federation rejection of $100 million business assistance package offered by the government. Ullrich said his opposition was

striking a chord with smaller exporters and manufacturers. He spoke last week to the Auckland Trade Centre, the Bay of Plenty branch of the Export Institute and is to address the Waikato Manufacturers Federation Branch. Page 19.
